description: issue #682 (Interaction & Events, slice I3): `when "start" [ ... ]` registers a named event handler and, because a batch run has already started, the standard `"start"` event is already being delivered, so the handler fires immediately after registration (spec/interaction-events.md's `### when <event-word> <block>`: registering "does not run its block immediately unless the triggering event is already being delivered"). The registration statement emits its own `instruction` event (seq 0), then the `primitive` event carrying only `name: "when"` is emitted AFTER the handler is registered (spec's "Trace stream integration": "Event registration forms emit `primitive` events after the handler is registered"), never the event word or any timing — the stream stays headless (spec/execution-model.md's trace-and-event registry). The handler block's start emits an `instruction` event for the block-head that caused it to run, carrying the `when` keyword's span (seq 2), then the body's `print` runs (seq 3-4). The `primitive` catch-all kind is registered by C5 (#694); M5 adds no new event kind.
